newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher with rising optimisem.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher with rising optimisem.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher for the second consecutive day on Thursday with traders saying that technical indicators supported the positive mood.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.43 percent, or 1.08 points, to 251.40 on high all-share turnover of 115 million shekels against 119 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.45 percent higher at 260.37.

"Investors gained confidence and the market looks good. Activity is rising and the mood has improved. This might even be the beginning of a new positive trend," said Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.
Another trader said investors are very optimistic since all the technical indicators show that the trend is positive.
"Even the options are reflecting hopes for a continued rise. The only thing that might ruin the party is the possibility of a sharp decline of the Dow," he added.
Weidelfeld said: "The market is rising slowly and the Maof broke the 260 level today with no problem which adds to investors' confidence."

Bezeq Israel Telecom fell 2.25 percent to 875 agorot. Israel's ministerial privatisation committee on Thursday approved a plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq, reducing its holding to 51 percent by the end of the year.
The news came as Bezeq's board announced it had named Ami Erel managing director.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries which fell 1.0 percent to 18,708 agorot on turnover of 6.1 million shekels and Koor Industries which lost 0.5 percent to 31,066 agorot on volume of 5.5 million shekels. Zannex Securities downgraded Koor on Thursday to a long-term buy from a buy.
Israel Chemicals, the third most active share, gained 2.5 percent to 375 on volume of 4.5 million shekels.
